title: Shoggoth wall art — round 04: synthesis
notes: 43 cards. First synthesis round: 7 generated concept comps of the actual piece (c01-c07, PREVIEW RESOLUTION — Canva credit quota blocked full-res export and concepts c08-c12; media ids logged in scratch prompts file, full-res re-export + 5 remaining comps queued for next round) + mask-treatment (m01-m12), plant-integration (p01-p12), depth-variance (v01-v12) reference groups. Mask group trawled by orchestrator inline — Sonnet worker pool hit account rate limit. Concept images live in this repo (generated content); reference images hotlinked.

cards.title: Concept: baseline — velvet salon install
cards.rationale: Baseline: dark velvet-salon install with graphic mask and plant-bearing spans.

cards.title: Concept: serene stone smile
cards.rationale: Tests mask language: sculpted serene stone smile vs graphic dots-and-curve.

cards.title: Concept: mask + toothy maw, ochre
cards.rationale: Tests sketch duality: clean graphic mask above separate toothy maw, ochre-dominant.

cards.title: Concept: studio raking light
cards.rationale: Tests surface legibility: bare dark wall, raking light, texture detail.

cards.title: Concept: rust corner wrap
cards.rationale: Tests palette (rust-dominant) and wall integration: tentacles wrapping an interior corner.

cards.title: Concept: Japanese minimal room, pothos
cards.rationale: Tests decor context: minimal dark Japanese room, piece as sole object, trailing pothos.

cards.title: Concept: rendered as Beksinski painting
cards.rationale: Tests medium: 2D Beksinski-style painting vs photoreal install.

cards.title: Bayon face towers, Angkor Thom
cards.rationale: Monumental serene stone smiles emerging from rough architecture; probes a sculpted-calm face reading as part of the mass rather than applied to it.

cards.title: Mask of Agamemnon, gold
cards.rationale: Serene hammered-gold death mask; probes a metallic contrast mask as the one clean element against a dark organic body.

cards.title: Noh masks in performance
cards.rationale: Pale serene ko-omote-type masks under stage light; probes the becalmed-face-on-dark-figure treatment (the anti-Hannya, which round-01 rejected).

cards.title: Budai, British Museum
cards.rationale: Jolly carved smile integral to a blobby organic body; probes smile-as-expression-of-the-mass vs smile-as-applied-mask.

cards.title: Greek comic actor with mask
cards.rationale: Ancient comedy mask held before a figure; probes the theatrical worn-mask convention — mask explicitly separate from the face beneath.

cards.title: Venetian carnival masks, amber
cards.rationale: Ornate clean masks displayed against dark ground; probes how decorative the mask surface can get before it fights the body's texture.

cards.title: Canonical smiley graphic
cards.rationale: The flat two-dots-and-curve icon itself, as drawn in the vision sketch; probes maximum graphic abstraction for the mask.

cards.title: Orcus mouth, Gardens of Bomarzo
cards.rationale: 16th-c. monster face whose maw is a door; probes the sketch's mask-above-maw duality executed at architectural scale.

cards.title: Sun and Moon faces, 17th-c. engraving
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: celestial folk faces — benign features applied to non-face objects; probes naive-folk linework for the mask.

cards.title: Jack-o'-lantern, vintage Hallowe'en print
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: grin carved into organic matter — the smile as a void/cutout rather than an applied plate.

cards.title: Smiley-face hammock installation
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: smiley as a functional object in space; probes the icon surviving translation into 3D structure.

cards.title: Bayon smile, close
cards.rationale: OUTLIER framing test: the same serene smile at intimate close range — monumental vs intimate read of a sculpted calm face.

cards.title: Emeric Chantier plant-covered figure sculptures — My Modern Met
cards.rationale: Can a creature body read as sculpture while living plants grow from it, and does foliage soften or amplify the horror?

cards.title: Monsieur Plant twisted bark-clad trunk sculptures — My Modern Met
cards.rationale: Does a dark bark-textured, knotted limb form work as the tentacle-span substrate that a flat shelf top is cut into?

cards.title: Giuseppe Licari root installation — designboom
cards.rationale: Do root-like tentacle forms read as organic support structure, with pots nested in the branching junctions?

cards.title: TevaPlanter self-watering wall tile planter — My Modern Met
cards.rationale: Planter as wall relief: how a sealed, self-watering tile hides waterproofing and soil in a flat wall composition.

cards.title: Epipremnum aureum (pothos), trailing habit — Wikipedia
cards.rationale: Trailing pothos cascading off a shelf edge: does a green drape over the dark tentacle read as lush contrast or visual clutter.

cards.title: Kokedama moss balls — Wikipedia
cards.rationale: Pot-free moss-ball plants hung or perched on the sculpture: removes ceramic pots, but does moss texture clash with calcified surface?

cards.title: Root-over-rock bonsai — Wikimedia Commons
cards.rationale: Roots gripping stone as a model for tentacle-gripping-pot geometry; tests a single small tree as shelf occupant.

cards.title: Green wall, Blusson Hall SFU — Wikipedia
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: full living wall as the artwork itself; tests whether Evan wants plants dominant over sculpture.

cards.title: Bosco Verticale, Milan — Wikipedia
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: protruding balconies carrying trees at scale; horizontal-protrusion variance as the planting structure.

cards.title: Sarracenia pitcher plants — Wikimedia Commons
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: carnivorous pitcher plants as the shelf occupants; vertical tubes read as predatory/horror-adjacent and need upward clearance.

cards.title: Fungi in art (mushroom statues) — Wikipedia
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: fungal/mycelium forms as the growth layer instead of foliage; tests bioart direction (live growth on sculpture).

cards.title: Naoki Onogawa bonsai trees of paper cranes — My Modern Met
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: bonsai as sculptural object (non-living stand-in); tests faux/preserved plants as a no-maintenance shelf fill.

cards.title: Gates of Hell — Rodin
cards.rationale: Figures go from flush bas-relief to nearly free-standing on one door plane; template for body-in-wall to tentacle-out-of-wall gradient.

cards.title: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa — Bernini
cards.rationale: Full-round marble figures cantilevered off a flat architectural niche with rays behind: how much mass can float before the wall reads as backdrop.

cards.title: Casa Batlló facade — Gaudí
cards.rationale: R02 liked Gaudí ('great great direction'): facade swells from flat plane to bone-like balconies with continuous depth gradient, no hard step.

cards.title: Pergamon Altar Gigantomachy frieze
cards.rationale: Hellenistic high relief with limbs and wings breaking the frame edge; writhing mass clustered, tests Ghiberti-plus-depth.

cards.title: Trevi Fountain — Salvi
cards.rationale: Sculpture bursting out of a flat palazzo wall; rock mass transitions from facade to freestanding horses and spills forward.

cards.title: El Transparente — Narciso Tomé, Toledo
cards.rationale: Baroque altar where figures burst through the wall and ceiling in layered depth planes with light behind; relief to full-round in one piece.

cards.title: Teatro Olimpico scaena — Palladio/Scamozzi
cards.rationale: False-perspective street receding in a few cm of depth: shallow relief can fake meters; could carry body detail in shallow wall depth while tentacles go truly deep.

cards.title: Matthew Shlian paper tessellations
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: folded paper wall relief where spikes jut from a flat sheet; pop-up engineering as a way to get big projection from flat stock, printable as folded-plate shells.

cards.title: Woven Image 3D-formed acoustic panels
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: acoustic diffuser wall with continuous peak/trough depth gradient; wall treatment that reads as sculpture, low-risk 'flat zone' vocabulary between deep spans.

cards.title: Climbing a Memory — Pavel Rotts, Helsinki
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: climbing wall cast from damaged architecture; load-rated protrusions on a flat wall, a real structural precedent for tentacle anchors and shelf loads.

cards.title: Automotive clay model — Opel design studio
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: full-size clay form half-resolved, surfaces scraped in planes; tests rough-sculpted unfinished emergence as a finish state.

cards.title: Ship figurehead — Aris (Tsamadou)
cards.rationale: OUTLIER: figure thrust forward from a flat hull plane as a single cantilever; the bow-mounted torso projection precedent for the mask or shelf-tentacle.
